topic: E-values, test martingales, betting-based confidence sequences applied to risk control, selective prediction, model certification, or deployment monitoring
method_notes: WebSearch with ten query formulations; every candidate's abstract read via arXiv before classification. The closest single object is Bai & Jin's SCoRE (e-value selective risk control, record-level exchangeability).

papers.title: Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control (SCoRE)
papers.why: The closest object found in this lane: constructs generalized e-values to give finite-sample, model-free error control on exactly the cases the system chooses to answer - the same certified-selective-prediction mechanism as CertGate's headline, including a covariate-shift extension. It stays record-level exchangeable: no site/cluster as the unit of independence, no BBSE label-shift mode with cluster-robust uncertainty, no explainable abstention, no pre-registered multi-site clinical validation. A reviewer will certainly expect this citation and a differentiation paragraph; the site-as-unit estimand is the load-bearing difference.

papers.title: Tracking the risk of a deployed model and detecting harmful distribution shifts
papers.why: The canonical anchor of this lane: time-uniform betting confidence sequences monitoring the risk of a deployed model and flagging harmful (vs benign) shifts with false-alarm control. Same statistical machinery (Waudby-Smith/Ramdas line) applied to deployment risk, but sequential monitoring rather than a one-shot certificate, no selective prediction, and records - not sites - are the independence unit. Expected citation in any e-value risk-control related-work section.

papers.title: Distribution-free uncertainty quantification for classification under label shift
papers.why: Direct precedent for CertGate's second assumption mode: BBSE-style importance reweighting of distribution-free UQ (conformal sets and calibration) under label shift, with unlabeled target data. It is conformal/calibration rather than a betting certificate, record-level rather than cluster-robust, and has no honest importance-weight budget that declines rather than overclaims. A reviewer scanning the BBSE-mode contribution will expect this cited and distinguished.

papers.title: On Continuous Monitoring of Risk Violations under Unknown Shift
papers.authors: Alexander Timans, Rajeev Verma, Eric Nalisnick, Christian A. Naesseth
papers.why: Testing-by-betting sequential procedure that detects violations of bounded risks for a deployed decision mechanism under unknown distribution shift, with false-alarm control - the monitoring-side mirror of CertGate's certificate, on the same e-process machinery. No selective prediction/abstention layer, no cluster-as-unit, no clinical multi-site validation.

papers.title: Selective Conformal Risk Control
papers.authors: Yunpeng Xu, Wenge Guo, Zhi Wei
papers.why: Two-stage framework integrating selective classification with conformal risk control on the selected subset, with exact finite-sample guarantees (SCRC-T). Overlaps the certified-selective-prediction component, but via conformal exchangeability arguments, not e-values/betting; record-level; no site clusters, label shift, or clinical multi-site data.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Confirmation of Label-Shift Corrections
papers.venue: ICML 2026 Workshop on Hypothesis Testing; arXiv 2606.14028
papers.why: Shows the per-observation likelihood ratio between a label-shift-corrected predictive and the source predictive is a conditional e-value, whose running product is a nonnegative martingale, giving anytime-valid confirmation of a posited label-shift correction. This is the exact intersection of CertGate's two statistical ingredients (e-value/martingale machinery + label-shift correction), though for confirming a correction rather than certifying answered-set error, with no selection, no clusters, no clinical data. Small workshop paper but directly on the seam.

papers.title: Conformal Selective Acting: Anytime-Valid Risk Control for RLVR-Trained LLMs
papers.why: Ville-type e-processes controlling SELECTIVE risk (explicitly distinguished from marginal risk) for act/abstain decisions on LLM output streams, with per-deployment error budgets and no pooling across deployments. Overlaps components (2) and the abstention framing; the setting is sequential LLM streams under an RLVR filtration - not exchangeable hospital sites as the independence unit, no label-shift mode, no clinical data.

papers.title: Certify or Refuse: A Cross-Model Map for Selective Risk Control with Coverage Floors under Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Jiamiao Liu, Dewen Qiao, Yu Zhang, Xuetao Chen
papers.why: Uses the same 'certified selective prediction' vocabulary - answer at least a beta-fraction while keeping answered-set error below alpha, with finite-sample sample-complexity bounds - under bounded-ratio covariate shift. No e-values/betting, no site-as-unit, QA benchmarks not clinical data, and covariate shift is explicitly out of CertGate's scope; still worth citing to disambiguate the overlapping terminology.

papers.title: Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets
papers.authors: Ziyu Xu, Nikos Karampatziakis, Paul Mineiro
papers.why: Extends risk-controlling prediction sets to the sequential setting via a wealth (betting) process, giving anytime-valid finite-sample risk control under a labeling budget. Same betting-for-risk-control machinery; differs in target (prediction-set risk over a stream with active labeling) and has no site clusters, abstention gate, or clinical validation.

papers.title: E-Values Expand the Scope of Conformal Prediction
papers.authors: Etienne Gauthier, Francis Bach, Michael I. Jordan
papers.why: Systematic treatment of conformal e-prediction: batch anytime-valid conformal prediction, fixed-size sets with data-dependent coverage, ambiguous ground truth. Establishes the e-value-for-distribution-free-UQ context a reviewer in this lane will have in mind; no selective risk control on an answered set, no clusters, no clinical setting.

papers.title: Adaptive auditing of AI systems with anytime-valid guarantees
papers.authors: Siyu Zhou, Patrick Vossler, Venkatesh Sivaraman, Yifan Mai, Jean Feng
papers.why: Testing-by-betting (SAVI) dueling e-processes for adaptively auditing whether an AI system has a failure mode below a performance threshold. Shows the betting-audit framing is active (Jean Feng's group also works on clinical AI monitoring), but it audits generative systems adaptively rather than certifying answered-set error, with no selection gate, clusters, or clinical data.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Risk Monitoring of Deployed Models for Detecting Harmful Distribution Shifts
papers.authors: Guangyi Zhang, Yunlong Cai, Guanding Yu, Osvaldo Simeone
papers.why: Semi-supervised anytime-valid lower bounds on running risk (prediction-powered inference plus time-uniform bounds) for detecting harmful shifts, extending the Podkopaev-Ramdas monitoring line. Assumption-free finite-sample type-I control, but monitoring not certification, no selection, no clusters, no clinical data.

papers.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
papers.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (with discussion); arXiv 2010.09686
papers.why: The foundational betting/e-value confidence-sequence construction the whole lane (and CertGate's certificate) descends from. Not a novelty threat - a methodological ancestor that must be cited; its finite-sample nonasymptotic bounds are what make a site-level n~208 certificate feasible at all.

papers.title: Game-theoretic statistics and safe anytime-valid inference
papers.authors: Aaditya Ramdas, Peter Grunwald, Vladimir Vovk, Glenn Shafer
papers.why: The survey that fixes the lane's vocabulary (e-values, e-processes, test martingales, Ville's inequality, optional stopping). Standard citation establishing that CertGate's certificate sits inside game-theoretic statistics; no overlap with the site-as-unit selective-prediction combination itself.
